headline: No fuel shortage in BD: Gas crisis may take 2 days to resolve
summary: The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources clarifies that fuel reserves are sufficient, while a technical glitch at an LNG terminal has caused a temporary gas supply dip.
details: The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources has assured the public that there is no shortage of fuel oil in Bangladesh, dismissing reports of a crisis as rumors aimed at creating panic.

During a press conference, Joint Secretary Monir Hossain Chowdhury stated that the country currently has 31 days of diesel, 36 days of octane, 20 days of petrol, 25 days of furnace oil, and 20 days of Jet fuel in reserve.
The ministry added that 180,000 tons of diesel are expected by July 31, with another 240,000 tons arriving in August, ensuring no fuel oil shortage for the next 48 days.

However, the ministry acknowledged a gas crisis. A technical fault at a floating LNG terminal (FSRU) has reduced the national grid's gas supply by approximately 450 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd).
This supply drop has affected industrial factories, power plants, CNG stations, and residential consumers, leading to long queues at some CNG stations.
Joint Secretary Monir Hossain assured that the technical issue is being repaired and the gas supply situation is expected to return to normal within two to three days.
The ministry noted that while the technical fault is the immediate cause, long-term reliance on imported LNG has made the system vulnerable to such infrastructure failures.
To reduce this dependency, the government has planned to drill 100 gas wells. A project to drill three new wells in Begumganj and Sunamganj has recently been approved with a budget of 729 crore BDT.
caption:
Fuel oil reserves are sufficient, but a technical glitch has hit the gas supply. Here is the latest from the Ministry.

The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources has assured the public that there is no shortage of fuel oil in Bangladesh, dismissing reports of a crisis as rumors aimed at creating panic.

During a press conference, Joint Secretary Monir Hossain Chowdhury stated that the country currently has 31 days of diesel, 36 days of octane, 20 days of petrol, 25 days of furnace oil, and 20 days of Jet fuel in reserve.

The ministry added that 180,000 tons of diesel are expected by July 31, with another 240,000 tons arriving in August, ensuring no fuel oil shortage for the next 48 days.

However, the ministry acknowledged a gas crisis. A technical fault at a floating LNG terminal (FSRU) has reduced the national grid's gas supply by approximately 450 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd).

This supply drop has affected industrial factories, power plants, CNG stations, and residential consumers, leading to long queues at some CNG stations.

Joint Secretary Monir Hossain assured that the technical issue is being repaired and the gas supply situation is expected to return to normal within two to three days.

The ministry noted that while the technical fault is the immediate cause, long-term reliance on imported LNG has made the system vulnerable to such infrastructure failures.

To reduce this dependency, the government has planned to drill 100 gas wells. A project to drill three new wells in Begumganj and Sunamganj has recently been approved with a budget of 729 crore BDT.

headline_marked: Up to $20,000: [[Bangladesh Bank eases forex rules for freelancers]]
headline: Up to $20,000: Bangladesh Bank eases forex rules for freelancers
summary: New guidelines allow for simpler payments and reduced documentation, supporting the growth of the digital services sector.
details: Bangladesh Bank has eased foreign exchange transaction rules for freelancers and individual service exporters to support the country's growing digital services sector.
Under the new circular, inward remittances of up to $20,000 can now be credited without formal declaration requirements, simplifying the process for small-value transactions.
Freelancers can now receive payments based on electronic evidence, such as platform statements and emails, removing the need for conventional export documentation.
Payments through online payment gateway service providers (OPGSPs) are permitted up to $10,000 per transaction, ensuring the timely repatriation of funds.
The central bank has also enabled the issuance of dual-currency freelancer cards and expanded the use of mobile financial services (MFS) and payment service providers (PSPs).
ICT sector freelancers may retain up to 50 percent of their export earnings in foreign currency accounts, while other service exporters can retain up to 30 percent.
Market participants believe this move aligns regulatory frameworks with the digital trade nature of freelance work, promoting formal remittance channels and transparency.
